summary: Without mature, independent gates this pattern is simply unreviewed machine output, and some legal, safety and organizational contexts require a named human decision regardless of automation quality.

points.text: AI review can share the author model's blind spots, training data and prompt assumptions; multiple correlated green verdicts do not create independent assurance.
Regulated or safety-critical changes may require segregation of duties, accountable approval or documented human judgment that a machine-only gate cannot satisfy.
Gate definitions erode under delivery pressure through skipped flaky tests, lowered thresholds and broad waivers; protecting and auditing gate configuration becomes a new critical review surface.
Small teams with low change volume may gain more from a fast human conversation than from building queues, evidence adapters, agent reviewers and audit sampling infrastructure.
